body.statement:
On the mixed center in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), use the quasi-uniform growing spline schedule in the narrowed boundary-likelihood claim, with \(J_n\to\infty\) and \(J_n\log n/n\to0\).  Then
\[
\inf_x\pi_0(x)=\frac12,\qquad
t_{0,n}\to\frac12,\qquad
h_{0,n}\to2,
\]
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}2<\frac12.
\]
Thus clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
body.justification: This recomputation removes the nonvanishing-clipping error created by allowing multipliers above one.
body.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
body.consumer: It verifies that the feasible rule targets the untrimmed control quantile on the explicit mixed-regime witness.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove uniform consistency and tail-regime classification of the actual bounded-arm constrained series fit under the proposed growing schedule.
obligation.obstruction: The population generalized inverse is elementary, but the empirical order statistic is a functional of the fitted propensity. No bounded-arm uniform likelihood theorem is presently a frozen or proved dependency.
obligation.attempted: Computed the population scale and the population log-boundary likelihood score for a fixed one-block fit. Its positive boundary coefficient supplies a direct counterexample to the original empirical order-statistic limits.
obligation.partial_result:
For the mixed law, \(F_0^\pi(t)=0\) for \(t\le1/2\), while \(F_0^\pi(t)>0\) for every \(t>1/2\).  Hence the generalized-inverse definition directly gives
\[
t_{0,n}\downarrow\frac12,\qquad h_{0,n}\to2.
\]
The empirical conclusions do not follow for an arbitrary allowed sieve schedule.  Indeed, take \(J_n\equiv1\), so that the bounded-arm fit contains an intercept and the required coefficient of \(\log(1-x)\).  At coefficient zero, the intercept-only fitted probability is
\[
E\{\pi_0(X)\}
=1-\frac12E(X^{3/2})
=1-\frac15
=\frac45.
\]
The population likelihood derivative in the log-boundary direction at this fit is
\[
\frac1{1-4/5}
E\!\left[\{\pi_0(X)-4/5\}\log(1-X)\right]>0,
\]
because \(\pi_0(X)\) and \(\log(1-X)\) are nonconstant decreasing functions of \(X\), and hence have strictly positive covariance.  Thus the population maximizer has a positive boundary coefficient.  Its fitted propensity approaches zero at the largest sample order statistics, rather than approaching the true lower endpoint \(1/2\).  Consequently the claimed fitted order-statistic limit fails.  A growing, uniformly consistent bounded-arm likelihood fit is therefore a necessary restriction; proving that fit for the actual constrained rule is the remaining step.
